Alabuga Start

By: Sibusisiwe Buthelezi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Alabuga Start markets itself as a program where female youth between the ages18-22 are given on the job training. The catch, the youth have to relocate to Russia.

Unique Selling Point:
We speak to two key players who are responsible for the program having a footprint in South Africa.

Summary:
What shot Alabuga into the spotlight in South Africa is a series of posts by South African influencers who claim they were
approached by an agency on behalf the program, to recruit young girls. When they were probed on what exactly the girls would be doing in Russia, they admitted that they did not know. After the public outrage where the influencers were accused of participating in Human Trafficking, they deleted the posts and have since issued public apologies.

Further enraging South Africans was that Cyan Boujie, a controversial influencer who is also known as a high-end “sex
worker”, was flown to Russia to give a virtual tour of Alabuga. She shared the video on all of her social media pages. This
further fuelled the suspicions of human trafficking for potential sex work in Russia.


Further information:
DIRCO has since denied having any knowledge of the program and said they were not working in partnership with the
Russian government. They also discouraged anyone from signing up for the program.

Press Release:


Alabuga Start 

A recruitment programme touted by local influencers promises jobs and training…the only condition: relocation to Russia. But as young women prepare to uproot their lives in the name of opportunity, suspicion flourishes. Influencers marketing the programme admit
they have no idea what the recruits will be doing overseas. When a public outcry accuses them of participating in human trafficking, they delete the posts and issue public apologies. Government issues a stern warning against the programme.
But who is really behind the drive to recruit young South African women to Russia? Carte Blanche investigates.

Producer: Sebe Buthelezi | Presenter: Masa Kekana  

Script:


(Seemah Mangolwane)- Have you ever imagined working abroad and getting a great
salary?
(Masa-) It was a Russian placement and training programme promising lucrative jobs; a
recruitment drive aided by popular South African influencers.
(Cyan Boujee)- Every six months brings a promotion, a salary increase and new
professional skills.
(Masa)- But online promises turned into real life drama.
(Crash Out Codey)- It’s not a secret that they are making drones in a factory.
(Masa)- Fingers have been pointed at so-called online influencers, but just who is
behind Russia’s Alabuga Start, a controversial scheme targeting the youth?
(Mzweleni Mthethwa)- Our main role was to recruit and be a partner who will assist
them to roll over the program. 
(Masa)- What research did you do?
(Siya Mhlungu)- I’m not going to engage in this further. 
(Clayson Monyela) The old saying remains true, if something looks too good to be true,
it probably is. 
(Alabuga)- Alabuga work and travel is a program that will help you realise yourself and
all your opportunities. 
(Masa)- Alabuga Start claims to offer paid jobs in a range of fields, from hospitality to
logistics. 
(Masa)- Targeting girls between 18 and 22, it arranges free training, accommodation
and flights.
(Masa)- The only condition: relocation to Russia. 
(Alabuga)- A career in Alabuga can be started with a cleaner of public spaces with a
salary of $500.
(Masa)- In South Africa, there’s a ready supply of potential candidates for Alabuga:
young people struggling to get into university or to find jobs. 
(Masa)- It’s a demographic that also spends a lot of time online. 
(Masa)- Following a series of social media posts by South African influencers
encouraging young girls aged between 18 and 22 to relocate to Russia, Alabuga Start
shot to the top of social media trends… for all the wrong reasons.
(Cyan Boujee)- I am in Russia, the Republic of Tartastan… Apparently girls are treated
fairly here. Africans, Asians, Latin American. 

(Masa)- These posts feature a local content creator known as Cyan Boujee. She was
the latest in a line of influencers spreading the Alabuga gospel.
(Masa)- But soon after they were posted late last month, disturbing reports emerged
about the true nature of the Russian programme.
(Masa)- It turns out, the influencers were recruiting for an alleged human trafficking
syndicate. 
(Masa)- The backlash – particularly online – was brutal.
(Seemah Mangolwane)- I really apologise for being so ignorant and putting young
women’s lives in danger, you know.
(Masa)- The apologies came thick and fast.
(Imsureits.hopey)- I am here to take accountability for my actions. 
 
(Bontle.le.Hlogi) It’s a mistake that we’ve made.
 
(Sasha)- The first thing I wanna do is apologise. 
(Masa)- At least three South African girls still in Russia have disputed the allegations
against Alabuga…
(Ingiphile)- whatever that is being said about human trafficking or whatever, I have no
idea about it.
(Masa)- But the controversy refuses to die down. Even our own International Relations
Department has been drawn into the fray.
(Clayson Monyela)- This would be a classic, for us at least given the information at our
disposal, where you are in an environment where you have to say what you are told to
say. 
(Masa)- If the Department’s Clayson Monyela is right, the question is: told by whom?
(Masa)- Could it be that the influencers have been unfairly blamed? What do we know
about Alabuga Start and is it connected to more than just a handful of online content
creators?
(Masa)- While South Africa and Russia do share a close relationship, the Department of
International Relations and Cooperation has made it abundantly clear they do not
endorse the Alabuga Start program, and it’s investigating it and all those involved.
(Masa)- Alabuga Start was launched to build a skilled workforce in a special economic
zone with the same name. Located in the centre of the Russian Federation, it targets
mainly young people from the developing world.
(Masa)- But the programme has become mired in allegations of human trafficking,
forced labour and poor working conditions.

(Masa)- It’s reported 200 women from around Africa were put to work in weapons
factories.
(Clayson Monyela)- This is not something that we are speculating over, we’ve got solid
evidence given the experiences of the people that we had to rescue.
(Masa) - Solid evidence to?
(Clayson Monyela)- To say that this is a scam, it’s not a legitimate job offer that South
Africans should consider. 
(Masa)- A student had to be rescued from the programme earlier this year.
(Clayson Monyela)- She got to that particular country and discovered that what was
promised and what was happening in reality are completely different. 
(Clayson Monyela)- And an official investigation was then triggered. 
(Masa)- Among those on the Department’s radar is a local digital marketing company
called Sway. It’s owned by this man: Siyabonga Mhlungu and is known for clinching
collaboration deals with influencers.
(Masa)- We were keen to find out what exactly Sway’s role had been in the Alabuga
saga.
(Siya Mhlungu)- There’s really nothing else that I can-
(Masa)- There’s a lot you can say. You’ve now become somewhat of the face of this. 
(Siya Mhlungu)- What am I clarifying exactly? 
(Masa)- Your role. The due diligence that you played before you promoted and
endorsed an alleged and possible human trafficking syndicate.
(Siya Mhlungu)- Can I just go back to my colleagues and update them.
(Masa)- Sure Siya, will you come back to us?
(Siya Mhlungu)- I will not run.
(Masa)- We wait, and wait and wait.
 
(Masa)- Eventually, we call him again. 
(Siya Mhlungu)- I’m saying that I’m just waiting to get the go-ahead.
(Masa)- Who is the owner of Sway Digital Siya?
(Siya Mhlungu)- I am. 

(Masa)- So why do you need a go-ahead from another organisation?
(Siya Mhlungu)- Because I said I was not going to do this interview today and they
convinced me.
(Masa)- With that, we stumble on a key player in this controversy – an obscure South
African based organisation calling itself the BRICS Student Commission.
(Masa)- BRICS is the inter-governmental organization that includes South Africa and
Russia – among others. According to Siya, the Student Commission is at the centre of
the Alabuga campaign, not him. 
(Masa)- What do you have to say about these allegations of human trafficking? Just tell
me that, because you are actually hiding behind other people.
(Masa)- There he goes, he’s hung up. He says he’s not avoiding accountability, yet he
doesn’t want to answer any questions.
(Masa)- As the Department of International Relations continued its own inquiry, our
investigation had taken an unexpected turn.
(Masa)- At first, what seemed like a controversy caused by paid influencers had
become far more obscure. And at its centre was a little-known commission claiming to
promote BRICS initiatives at institutions of higher learning.
(Masa)- Its president, Mzweleni Mthethwa, admitted that the commission has been
helping Alabuga establish a presence in South Africa.
(Mzweleni Mthethwa)- It was 2024 November, where we signed an MOU with them.
(Masa)- So when they said girls between 18 and 22 you don't find that to be
concerning? You didn't find that to be suspicious because only girls?
(Mzweleni Mthethwa)- We also queried that, why this age? Why these people, why this
gender? They had to give us an explanation to say people between this age, they are
still young and will have to learn another language there.
(Masa)- Did they tell you they'd be working in a factory making drones? Allegedly? 
(Mzweleni Mthethwa)- We were not told that, only four aspects that were covered, and
they were all under the driver in the hospitality space. 
(Masa)- All that proves is that you didn’t do your research. You went and signed an
MOU without doing due diligence. That's the bottom line.
(Mzweleni Mthethwa)- We had to do due diligence in terms of human right, in terms of
working hours, in terms of everything.
(Masa)- Our own diligence left us with more questions than answers. 

(Masa)- The Student Commission’s website features just three articles, all of them
written last year. 
(Masa)- And oddly, the BRICS hyperlink leads to a page that can’t be opened. 
(Masa)- Are you affiliated with the Department of International Relations and
Cooperation?
(Mzweleni Mthethwa)- Yes, from time to time, we do engage them.
(Clayson Monyela)- There is no private entity that can be affiliated with us. We are
government.
(Masa)- Monyela says, once their investigation is complete, the BRICS Student
Commission, Sway Digital’s Siya Mhlungu and the influencers will be held accountable.
(Clayson Monyela)- You will have to explain to the security agencies that are ceased
with this investigation why are you promoting this thing, what do you know about it, why
you are endorsing it
(Masa)- And for those who say look, I didn’t know?
(Clayson Monyela)- Well unfortunately when it comes to legal matters, ignorance of the
law is never an excuse that’s acceptable.
(Masa)- Despite multiple attempts, our efforts to get a response from Alabuga itself were
futile. 
(Masa)- The 3 South African girls are still in Russia, while Dirco continues to investigate
if there are more who are waiting to be rescued.

(Masa)- These posts feature a local content creator known as Cyan Boujee. She was the latest in a line of influencers spreading the Alabuga gospel. (Masa)- But soon after they were posted late last month, disturbing reports emerged about the true nature of the Russian programme. (Seemah Mangolwane)- I really apologise for being so ignorant and putting young women’s lives in danger, you know. (Masa)- The apologies came thick and fast. (Imsureits.hopey)- I am here to take accountability for my actions. (Bontle.le.Hlogi) It’s a mistake that we’ve made. (Sasha)- The first thing I wanna do is apologise. (Masa)- If the Department’s Clayson Monyela is right, the question is: told by whom? (Masa)- Could it be that the influencers have been unfairly blamed? What do we know about Alabuga Start and is it connected to more than just a handful of online content creators? (Masa)- While South Africa and Russia do share a close relationship, the Department of International Relations and Cooperation has made it abundantly clear they do not endorse the Alabuga Start program, and it’s investigating it and all those involved. (Masa)- Alabuga Start was launched to build a skilled workforce in a special economic zone with the same name. Located in the centre of the Russian Federation, it targets mainly young people from the developing world. (Masa)- But the programme has become mired in allegations of human trafficking, forced labour and poor working conditions. (Masa)- It’s reported 200 women from around Africa were put to work in weapons factories. (Clayson Monyela)- This is not something that we are speculating over, we’ve got solid evidence given the experiences of the people that we had to rescue. (Masa) - Solid evidence to? (Clayson Monyela)- To say that this is a scam, it’s not a legitimate job offer that South Africans should consider. (Masa)- A student had to be rescued from the programme earlier this year. (Clayson Monyela)- She got to that particular country and discovered that what was promised and what was happening in reality are completely different. (Clayson Monyela)- And an official investigation was then triggered. (Masa)- Among those on the Department’s radar is a local digital marketing company called Sway. (Siya Mhlungu)- Can I just go back to my colleagues and update them. (Masa)- Sure Siya, will you come back to us? (Siya Mhlungu)- I will not run. (Masa)- We wait, and wait and wait. (Masa)- At first, what seemed like a controversy caused by paid influencers had become far more obscure. And at its centre was a little-known commission claiming to promote BRICS initiatives at institutions of higher learning. You didn't find that to be suspicious because only girls? (Mzweleni Mthethwa)- We also queried that, why this age? Why these people, why this gender? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Alabuga Start markets itself as a program where female youth between the ages18-22 are given on the job training. The catch, the youth have to relocate to Russia.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We speak to two key players who are responsible for the program having a footprint in South Africa.
metadata.Summary: What shot Alabuga into the spotlight in South Africa is a series of posts by South African influencers who claim they were approached by an agency on behalf the program, to recruit young girls. When they were probed on what exactly the girls would be doing in Russia, they admitted that they did not know. After the public outrage where the influencers were accused of participating in Human Trafficking, they deleted the posts and have since issued public apologies. Further enraging South Africans was that Cyan Boujie, a controversial influencer who is also known as a high-end “sex worker”, was flown to Russia to give a virtual tour of Alabuga. She shared the video on all of her social media pages. This further fuelled the suspicions of human trafficking for potential sex work in Russia.
metadata.Further information: DIRCO has since denied having any knowledge of the program and said they were not working in partnership with the Russian government. They also discouraged anyone from signing up for the program.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: Boardroom for Zoom interview with Brics Commission
metadata.Reason for legal: We will be holding to account Alabuga Start, Brics Student Alliance as well as Sway Digital Marketing.
metadata.Reason for graphics: The story happens online so we will need a look and feel that makes the story seem as though it is unfolding online.
